label: token d input at step 0 or 1
explanation: Fires exactly when the input token is the letter d at one of the first two original positions (t=0 or t=1). Magnitude is set by position: at t=0 it is always at max (~3.6, 74.5% of mass); at t=1 it is much weaker (~0.28-0.42 of max, ~1.0-1.5), varying with the preceding token (e.g. b before d gives ~0.42, i/t give ~0.28). Does not fire on d at t>=2, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including copy-phase d outputs fed back). One negligible exception in dev (a d at step 4, activation ~0).

issues: Test split has 2 missed activations, both in the copy phase at step 4 of L=3 sequences where d is the recalled token fed back as input (activation 0.01 and 0.03 of max). That makes 'never fires in the copy phase, including when d comes back' a slight overclaim, but these hold 0.0% of activation mass. They are negligible noise, not a systematic class.

Dev profile agrees with the claims: d is 100% of activation mass, t=0 carries 74.5% and t=1 carries 25.5%, and there is no activity at t>=2, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase apart from 1 step. Active counts at t=0 and t=1 are almost equal, so the mass ratio implies t=1 runs at about 0.34 of the t=0 level, which fits the 0.28-0.42 range claimed. I did not check the specific claim that the preceding token sets the t=1 level.
